title: Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint — Experiment Framework & Guardrails
author: Sana Farid
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the experimentation standards for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (emails, in-console nudges, and retargeting). It is the source of truth for:
- Randomization units and assignment rules
- Holdout strategy
- Minimum run-time and sample size heuristics
- Dashboards and reporting expectations
- Decision thresholds (ship / iterate / rollback)
- Guardrails (deliverability, support load, and product performance)

This framework is designed to keep results interpretable while minimizing user harm and operational risk.

## Scope
Applies to all sprint experiments that target self-serve and PLG-led developers, including:
1) Onboarding email sequences (welcome → first success → troubleshooting → next steps)
2) In-console nudges (activation checklist, contextual banners, just-in-time prompts)
3) Retargeting campaigns (LinkedIn/Google) for non-activated signups and recently lapsed users

## Definitions
- **Activation (primary milestone for this sprint):** `first_request_success` (first 2xx response from a Redwood inference endpoint) within the measurement window.
- **Time-to-first-success (TTFS):** time between `signup_completed` and `first_request_success`.
- **Early retention:** D7 and D14 repeat product usage (see event taxonomy for canonical retention events).
- **Guardrail:** metric that, if violated, triggers pause/rollback regardless of primary metric performance.

Refer to the canonical event names and required properties in: `product-docs/requirements/event-taxonomy-activation-retention`.

---

## Randomization & Assignment
### Guiding principles
- **Sticky assignment:** a user should remain in the same variant for the experiment duration.
- **Single source of assignment:** the Console experimentation middleware is the authority for console experiences; Marketing Ops tooling is the authority for email/ads. We must avoid contradictory variant assignment across systems.
- **Minimize interference:** do not run two experiments that change the same step in the activation path for the same user at the same time unless explicitly designed as a factorial test.

### Randomization units (by channel)
**1) In-console nudges**
- **Randomization unit:** `user_id` (preferred) with a safeguard to pin to `workspace_id` for shared workspaces when multiple users are active.
- **Assignment:** server-side bucketing via experiment assignment middleware (sticky bucketing + holdouts).
- **Exposure logging:** emit `experiment_exposure` event at first render of the component in an eligible session.

**2) Onboarding emails**
- **Randomization unit:** `user_id` (or email hash when user_id is unavailable at send time).
- **Assignment:** performed in the email orchestration system; variant id must be passed through UTMs and stamped into downstream product events where possible.
- **Suppression alignment:** email assignment must respect global suppression rules (unsubscribe, complaint, and “do-not-email” flags).

**3) Retargeting ads**
- **Randomization unit:** platform audience membership (hashed email list / advertising ids), with holdout where supported.
- **Assignment:** audience split into treatment vs holdout lists (see holdout section).
- **Attribution:** click-through attribution will be directional; primary outcomes must still be evaluated in product events when the user returns.

### Eligibility rules (must be explicit per experiment)
Each experiment entry in the tracker must specify:
- Target segment (e.g., new self-serve signups, lapsed users, SDK users)
- Inclusion start time (e.g., from signup timestamp, or “first seen in last 14 days”)
- Exclusion criteria (enterprise-managed domains if required, internal/test accounts, existing activated users for activation-focused nudges)

---

## Holdouts
### Default holdout policy
Unless otherwise approved:
- **Console nudges:** 10% holdout (no new nudges shown) for all eligible users.
- **Email sequence:** 5–10% holdout (receives baseline transactional emails only; no lifecycle series).
- **Retargeting:** 10% holdout (excluded from retargeting audiences), where platform constraints allow.

### Why we keep holdouts
- Protects against seasonality and correlated external factors.
- Enables incremental lift measurement (especially where attribution is noisy).

### Holdout caveats
- Holdout users still count for guardrails and performance monitoring.
- If an experiment materially changes the product surface area (e.g., new checklist UI), ensure holdout users are not inadvertently exposed through caching or shared workspace state.

---

## Sample Size & Run-Time Heuristics
### Minimum runtime
- **Minimum run-time:** 7 full days after ramp to capture weekday/weekend behavior.
- **Preferred run-time:** 14 days for retention reads (D7), unless traffic is high enough to reach power earlier.
- Do not stop experiments early due to “promising” results unless a guardrail is violated (early stopping biases results).

### Power / MDE heuristics (rule-of-thumb)
Because signup volume and channel mix fluctuate, we use a rule-of-thumb approach unless we run a formal power calculation:
- Target **80% power** to detect a **5–10% relative lift** in activation rate.
- For activation-rate experiments, aim for **≥ 1,000 eligible users per arm** before calling a decision “ship” (unless effect size is large and consistent across cuts).
- For retention (D7/D14), expect larger sample requirements; use retention reads primarily for directional confirmation during this sprint.

### Unit of analysis
- Default unit is **user** (not session, not request).
- Ensure each user is counted once per metric window.

---

## Metrics & Decision Thresholds
### Primary metrics (per PRD)
- **Activation rate within 24h and 72h** of signup
- **TTFS** (median; also track P75/P90)
- **D7 and D14 retention** (repeat usage)
- **Higher-intent milestones:** `billing_added`, token usage growth, `route_created`, `teammate_invited`

### Guardrail metrics (global)
- Email deliverability and unsubscribes
- Support ticket volume and escalation rate
- Console performance (latency, errors) and SLO impacts

### Decision rubric
We use the following rubric at readout. “Ship” requires both primary metric improvement and no guardrail violations.

**Ship (roll-forward)**
- Primary metric improves by **≥ +3 percentage points** OR **≥ +8% relative** (whichever is more conservative for the segment),
- Result is directionally consistent across at least two key cuts (e.g., region and SDK),
- Guardrails are within thresholds,
- No material qualitative user harm identified by Support/CS.

**Iterate (keep running / adjust copy / adjust triggers)**
- Primary metric is flat to mildly positive but below ship threshold,
- Strong evidence of improvement in a leading indicator (e.g., TTFS improves but activation rate is flat),
- No guardrail violations,
- Clear next hypothesis (e.g., reduce friction on auth errors).

**Rollback / stop**
- Primary metric declines materially (e.g., activation down ≥ 2pp), OR
- Any guardrail threshold is violated, OR
- Significant user confusion / trust impact reported by Sales/CS.

### Statistical reporting standard
- Provide absolute values and deltas, not just percent lift.
- Include confidence intervals (or Bayesian credible intervals) for the primary metric.
- Do not over-interpret subsegment cuts unless the sample size supports it; subsegment reads are diagnostic, not primary.

---

## Dashboards & Reporting
### Required dashboards (by owner)
**Product analytics (Activation funnel)** — Owner: Mei Lin / Logan Wright
- Funnel: signup → api key created → first request success → first streaming success → dashboard viewed
- Slices: region, SDK (TS/Python/other), model family, new vs returning, traffic source (UTM)

**Attribution & channel performance** — Owner: Tyler Benson
- Email: delivered, open, click, unsubscribe, complaint, bounce
- Retargeting: spend, impressions, CTR, landing-page CVR, assisted conversions (directional)

**Console performance & reliability** — Owner: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant
- Console web vitals (p75 LCP/INP where available), API error rates, p95 route latency for key endpoints
- Error banner click rates and support-link click rates (as early warning)

### Standard experiment reporting format
Every experiment readout must include:
- Hypothesis and what changed
- Eligibility + randomization unit + holdout
- Timeline and ramp details
- Primary metric results with intervals
- Guardrail checks
- Key qualitative feedback (Support/Sales snippets)
- Decision + follow-ups

Use the sprint readout template in Drive: `google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/sprint-readout-template`.

---

## Guardrails (Thresholds & Actions)
Guardrails are evaluated daily during ramp and at least 2–3x per week thereafter.

### 1) Email deliverability & compliance
Owner: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)

**Thresholds (pause and investigate if triggered):**
- Unsubscribe rate: **> 1.0%** per send OR **2× baseline** for the same segment
- Spam complaint rate: **> 0.08%** per send
- Hard bounce rate: **> 1.0%**
- Significant deliverability degradation (e.g., inbox placement drop flagged by tooling, or sudden delivered-rate decline)

**Actions:**
1. Pause the problematic step (specific email) before pausing the entire sequence.
2. Verify suppression rules and opt-out handling (especially for re-sends and follow-ups).
3. Audit links/UTMs and destination correctness (avoid broken links/404s).
4. Escalate to Security/Compliance if opt-out behavior is incorrect (see related page: marketing tracking data review).

### 2) Support volume and severity
Owner: Dev Patel (Support guardrails lead)

**Thresholds:**
- Support tickets tagged “onboarding/activation” increase **> 25% week-over-week** during the experiment window
- Any **P1/P2** support issue attributable to experiment changes (e.g., incorrect billing prompts, broken console navigation)
- Repeated reports of confusion attributable to copy/claims (Sales/CS feedback)

**Actions:**
1. Triage and label tickets with experiment id (where possible).
2. If systemic, pause experiment exposure and ship a copy fix.
3. Provide an internal FAQ update for Sales/CS if messaging is causing inbound confusion.

### 3) Console performance and SLO impact
Owner: Sean Gallagher (SLO/guardrails)

**Thresholds:**
- Console page load regression: **p75 LCP +200ms** (or equivalent performance budget metric) sustained for >24h
- Console API error rate: **+0.3pp** above baseline sustained for >1h during peak
- Any measurable increase in inference request error rates attributable to onboarding flow changes (e.g., bad copy causing malformed requests)

**Actions:**
1. Roll back via feature flag (console nudges are required to be flag-guarded).
2. Confirm experiment exposure logging is not creating hot paths.
3. Coordinate with Console Eng for hotfix if instrumentation is malformed or overly chatty.

---

## Ramps, Rollbacks, and Change Control
### Ramp guidelines
- Begin at **10%** exposure for console nudges for 4–24 hours while monitoring guardrails.
- Increase to **50%** after initial validation; then to target (typically 90% treatment / 10% holdout).
- Emails and retargeting can ramp by cohort/time window (e.g., “new signups starting Monday”).

### Rollback requirements
- Console nudges must be safe to disable immediately via feature flag.
- Email steps must be independently pausable.
- Retargeting audiences must support quick removal of high-risk segments.

### Change log
Each experiment must log:
- Variant ids and copy version
- Trigger logic changes
- Exposure definition changes
- Start/stop timestamps

---

## Data Quality Requirements (Non-negotiable)
Before counting an experiment as “live,” confirm:
- `experiment_exposure` is emitted exactly once per user per experiment (or clearly documented if multi-exposure is intentional).
- Primary funnel events are firing and include required identifiers/properties.
- UTM capture is populating the agreed event properties where applicable.
- Internal/test accounts are excluded from analysis.

If instrumentation is found to be incorrect post-launch, document the impacted window and either:
- exclude the window from analysis, or
- re-run the experiment after fixing instrumentation.

---

## Owners & Escalation
- Framework/statistics: Sana Farid
- Event taxonomy & schema validation: Logan Wright
- Email deliverability & suppression: Tyler Benson
- Console experiment infra: Jada Williams / Jin Woo Park
- Console SLO/guardrails: Sean Gallagher
- Support guardrails: Dev Patel

Escalation path for any guardrail breach:
1) Post in #general and #product with experiment id and symptom
2) Pause exposure (flag / email step / audience)
3) Open a tracking ticket and assign to the experiment owner + relevant platform owner

---

## Appendix: Required fields in the Experiment Tracker
Each experiment row must include (at minimum):
- Experiment ID + name
- Owner
- Channel (email / console / retargeting)
- Eligibility and exclusions
- Randomization unit
- Holdout percentage
- Variant definitions
- Primary metric + window
- Guardrails to monitor
- Start date / planned end date
- Status (planned / ramping / running / paused / complete)

See: `google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/experiment-tracker`.
